claims.title: The global finite-mixture TV modulus is two-Lipschitz under maximum rowwise TV perturbation
claims.scope: finite categorical channels K,K' with matched rows satisfying max_i TV(K_i,K_i')<=epsilon
assumptions: the same latent row labels are matched across channels
nonclaims: the bound need not be tight for nonuniform row radii

claims.title: The factor two in rowwise TV stability is sharp
claims.scope: binary identity channel with both rows moved inward by epsilon in [0,1/2]
assumptions: standard total variation on a binary observed alphabet

claims.title: Row-specific uncertainty yields an exact zero-sum lower certificate for every disjoint-face separation
claims.scope: finite categorical channel with one declared TV radius per component row
assumptions: nominal face event games are complete
penalized exact rational game searches complete below caps
nonclaims: the robust lower certificate is not asserted equal to the worst admissible channel modulus for arbitrary coupled row perturbations

claims.title: A positive facewise robust modulus certifies identifiability and inverse conditioning uniformly over the rowwise channel uncertainty set
claims.scope: finite rowwise-TV channel uncertainty sets with positive robust lower modulus
assumptions: the true channel lies inside every declared row TV ball
nonclaims: zero lower bound means no certificate, not universal nonidentifiability

claims.title: Uniform row uncertainty epsilon preserves a certified modulus max(0,alpha-2epsilon)
claims.scope: finite categorical channels with the same TV radius epsilon on every row
assumptions: all disjoint-face games are enumerated exactly
nonclaims: epsilon<alpha/2 is sufficient for robust identifiability, not a universal necessary condition under structured perturbations

claims.title: Identity K3 with uncertainty only on one row has facewise robust modulus three-quarters versus coarse lower bound one-half
Half-TV uncertainty around the binary identity channel permits exact row collapse and loss of identifiability
claims.scope: binary identity channel with radius one-half on each row
assumptions: the midpoint row is admissible for both components
nonclaims: smaller structured uncertainty sets may retain identifiability

claims.title: Bounded exact row-uncertain finite-mixture conditioning audit
claims.scope: binary sharpness, exact collapse, asymmetric K3, uniform near-midpoint uncertainty, latent-radius transfer, and invalid-radius rejection
assumptions: all nominal and penalized exact game searches complete below caps
all values use exact rational arithmetic
nonclaims: bounded tests are not a scalability theorem
CI success is not evidence for simulation
